method_notes: Candidate pages checked via Wikimedia Commons API (license + author + size read from file metadata; canonical page = https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/<File title>) and Pexels pages. Clip contents were NOT watched frame by frame: usable-moment counts are estimates from titles/descriptions/durations (null where unknown). Commons PD tag is a pointer, rights-scout must still verify the primary source (Library of Congress, NOAA, NASA). Competitor evidence comes from third-party listings (vling.net) with unverified counts.

competitor_gap_evidence.note: Funny Ranking: Top 5 funniest moments from across the internet (repost model). Page did not render for fetch; description via search snippet only.
AttentionShorts: ranks funniest moments/fails/unexpected clips from YouTube Shorts; ~299 subs, 17 videos (third-party, unverified).
Fail-channel space dominated by social/UGC repost channels; no rights-clear public-domain angle seen.
Media interest in 'deep-sea animals meet a sub' angle; no ranking Short found in searches.
Astronauts-falling-on-Moon supercut got press; existing supercuts are unranked/unnarrated.

ideas.hard_gate_notes: Rights strong (pre-1930, 1890s) but verify each film's primary archive. Edison clips are 320x240: 9:16 crop will be soft, lean into 'old film' look; Lumiere clips are 1000+ px. Check restored/uploader overlays and any added music/intertitles on Commons versions (use the film, not a modern score). Avoid period racial caricature (some Edison titles, e.g. Chinese Laundry, excluded).

Pilot blocker until a higher-res source is confirmed. Avoid news-network overlays and the Apollo 11 TV pool footage (producer mixes).
